{{Short description|American mathematician (1919-1975)}}
'''Anthony Francis Bartholomay''' (1919–1975) was an American mathematician who introduced [[molecular set theory]], a topic on which he wrote books.

==Life==
Bartholomay was born on August 11, 1919. He would receive degrees from [[Hamilton College]], [[Syracuse University]], and [[Harvard University]]. Bartholomay would work at [[Harvard Medical School]], [[University of Toledo|Medical School of Ohio]], [[Brown University]], [[Keuka College]], [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]], and [[Rutgers University]].<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Bulletin of Mathematical Biology |last1=Karreman |first1=George |title=Obituary - Anthony Francis Bartholomay |doi=10.1007/BF02470617 |s2cid=117392087 |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF02470617.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218200429/https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF02470617.pdf |archive-date=February 18, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> He died on March 21, 1975, at 55 years old. A resident of the [[Somerset, New Jersey|Somerset]] section of [[Franklin Township, Somerset County, New Jersey]], he died at a [[New Brunswick, New Jersey]] hospital from a [[stroke]] he had three weeks prior to his death.<ref>Staff. [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=19750325&id=2BZPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=OAIEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7549,3963594&hl=en "Dr. Anthony Bartholomay Former Member of MCO Facility"], ''[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|Toledo Blade]]'', March 25, 1975. Accessed May 14, 2016.</ref>

==Molecular set theory==
Molecular set theory (MST) is a mathematical formulation of the wide-sense chemical kinetics of biomolecular reactions in terms of sets of molecules and their chemical transformations represented by set-theoretical mappings between molecular sets.

==Career==
Bartholomay was a professor and chairman of the Department of Mathematical Medicine at the [[Medical College of Ohio]].<ref>Thomas Tryniski 309 South 4th Street Fulton NY. "Professor, Utica Native, Dies in N.J." ''Old Fulton NY Post Cards By Tom Tryniski'' (n.d.): n. pag. Web.</ref> He was only part of the Department of Mathematical Medicine from 1969 until 1972, when he left. The department subsequently collapsed the following year.

[[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] website had Anthony Bartholomay listed as an investigator but was hosted at [[Harvard Medical School]] in 1957.<ref>"Anthony F. Bartholomay, SD | HHMI.org." ''HHMI.org''. N.p., n.d. Web. 31 Oct. 2015.</ref>
